column2: Architectural cutaway cross-section illustration of the entire volcano, like a museum infographic poster. A hot spring rises at the crater and flows DOWN through the mountain level by level, shown with glowing teal water paths and arrows. Label each level in clean English text from top to bottom: "CALDERA CROWN INFINITY POOL", "CASCADE TERRACES", "GUEST SUITES", "MIST CORRIDORS", "KAWAGIRI RESTAURANT over the underground river", "AQUA CAVERN WATER PARK", and at the very bottom a sealed "MAGMA VIEWING CHAMBER" glowing orange behind glass. Small human figures for scale. Dark charcoal background, teal and amber accents, title "KAZAN-YU — THE DESCENT".

Top-down architectural master floor plan of the KAZAN-YU cave spa, drawn like a luxury architect's presentation board on dark charcoal paper with fine white linework, teal-filled water areas and amber light points. Organic cave chambers connected by narrow reflecting-pool corridors. Clearly labeled zones: "ARRIVAL GATE", "MIST CORRIDORS", "CHANGING HALLS", "KAWAGIRI RESTAURANT", "UNDERGROUND RIVER", "AQUA CAVERN (10 attractions)", "STEAM GROTTO", "ICE CAVE PLUNGE", "TREATMENT ROOMS", "PRIVATE SUITES". North arrow, scale bar, legend, title block "KAZAN-YU — LEVEL B1 MASTER PLAN".

The arrival hall: guests in indigo yukata pass through a massive torii gate carved from black basalt into a high cave hall. One wall is a floor-to-ceiling slab of thick glass with slow orange lava glowing far behind it. A wall of wooden slipper cubbies, a stone basin with a bamboo water spout, steam drifting, hanging lantern clusters. Sense of awe and calm.

The "Kiri-no-Michi" mist corridors: a narrow winding cave hallway whose entire floor is a shallow ankle-deep reflecting pool of still dark water, with flat stepping stones flush beneath the surface. A thick low layer of white mist rolls knee-high over the water. Barefoot guests in yukata walk through holding their hems. Basalt walls with tiny lanterns set into niches, reflections doubling every light. Dreamlike, serene.

KAWAGIRI, a fantasy over-the-top luxury Japanese restaurant built inside a huge cave, suspended on heavy dark wooden beams and posts over a fast flowing glowing turquoise underground river. Each table sits on its own wooden platform, separated from the next by a thin falling sheet of water acting as a privacy screen curtain. Tiny wooden aqueducts on stilts weave between the tables. Lowkey moody atmosphere: magenta and cyan neon kanji signs, red lanterns, steam rising from bowls, mist off the river below. Wide establishing shot.

Architectural plan and section drawing sheet of the KAWAGIRI restaurant, presentation style on dark charcoal paper. LEFT: top-down plan showing the underground river flowing through the middle, a timber deck on beams above it, 12 private table pods each enclosed by "WATER CURTAIN" screens, a central "RAMEN COUNTER" and "KITCHEN", and a branching network of thin lines labeled "SOY AQUEDUCT" and "TEA AQUEDUCT" feeding every table. RIGHT: a cross-section showing the river below, the beams, a table pod with water falling from a ceiling trough into a floor gutter. Clean English labels, teal water, amber and neon-magenta accents.

Close-up of a single private dining table at KAWAGIRI. A miniature hand-carved hinoki wood aqueduct, like a tiny Roman aqueduct crossed with Japanese bamboo kakei, arrives at the table edge: one channel trickles dark soy sauce into a small ceramic dish, a second channel pours steaming green tea into a cup via a tiny bamboo spout. Behind the table a glistening sheet of falling water forms a privacy curtain, catching magenta and cyan neon light. A bowl of ramen steaming. Shallow depth of field, intimate and magical.

A lowkey neon ramen counter deep in the cave restaurant: a long worn wooden counter with a chef in a white headband pulling noodles, tall steam plumes, hanging noren curtains, glowing magenta and cyan neon signs reading "ラーメン" and "火山", red paper lanterns, wet stone floor reflecting neon. A signature "Lava Tonkotsu" bowl in front with a glowing chili oil swirl and a soft egg. Cozy late-night Tokyo alley feeling but inside a volcano.

Illustrated isometric fantasy map of "AQUA CAVERN", a spa water park inside a giant volcanic cave, in the style of a luxury resort guide map. Ten clearly numbered attractions with English labels: "1 CALDERA CROWN INFINITY POOL", "2 LAVA TUBE LAZY RIVER", "3 MAGMA GLASS SLIDE", "4 GEYSER PLAZA", "5 OBSIDIAN MIRROR FLOAT POOL", "6 FUMAROLE STEAM GROTTO", "7 GLACIER PLUNGE ICE CAVE", "8 RIMSTONE CASCADE TERRACES", "9 THUNDER CURTAIN FALLS", "10 WAVE GROTTO". Hot water visibly cascading from the top attraction down to the lower ones. Teal water, black basalt, amber lanterns.

Attraction 1, CALDERA CROWN INFINITY POOL: an infinity hot spring pool carved into the very rim of the volcano crater at night, its edge vanishing into a sea of clouds below, stars and a full moon above, steam rising, teal glowing water spilling over the edge and beginning its journey down the mountain. A few guests leaning on the edge, lanterns along the rim.

Attraction 2, LAVA TUBE LAZY RIVER: guests drift on dark woven floating rings along a warm turquoise river winding through a perfectly round ancient lava tube tunnel. The ceiling is ribbed basalt with glowing amber cracks and thousands of tiny blue glowworm lights. Mist on the water, lanterns floating alongside.

Attraction 3, MAGMA GLASS SLIDE: a transparent glass tube water slide spiraling down through a vast chamber, passing directly beside a wall of thick glass behind which real orange molten lava slowly flows. A rider silhouetted inside the tube, water and bubbles lit orange. Thrilling and dramatic, but luxurious.

Attraction 4, GEYSER PLAZA: a circular cave plaza with a shallow warm pool and a ring of carved stone seats; natural geysers erupt in timed sequence through openings in the floor, shooting columns of steaming water to the ceiling, lit teal from below. Guests laughing as spray falls. A rock skylight opening shows the night sky.

Attraction 5, OBSIDIAN MIRROR FLOAT POOL: a perfectly still, extremely dense mineral-salt float pool in a black obsidian chamber; the water is a flawless black mirror. The domed ceiling is covered in glowworms like a galaxy, and the mirror doubles them so floating guests appear suspended in space. Silent, meditative, a few lanterns at the edge.

Attraction 6, FUMAROLE STEAM GROTTO: a series of interconnected small steam caves graded in heat, natural volcanic vents releasing thick white steam, carved basalt benches, hinoki wood ladles and buckets, amber light filtering through the steam in god rays, guests wrapped in towels. Hanging signs with temperatures "45°", "55°", "65°".

Attraction 7, GLACIER PLUNGE ICE CAVE: an astonishing contrast cave — a cold plunge pool inside a cave of translucent glowing blue glacier ice that meets the black volcanic basalt; meltwater drips from icicles; a warm amber doorway on one side leads back to the steam. A guest stepping down stone stairs into the icy water, breath visible.

Attraction 8, RIMSTONE CASCADE TERRACES: a cavern of natural travertine-like rimstone terraces, dozens of scalloped stepped pools pouring into each other down a slope inside the volcano, each pool slightly cooler than the one above. Teal glowing water, white mineral rims against black basalt, guests lounging in individual pools, lanterns on the rims.

Attraction 9, THUNDER CURTAIN FALLS: a massive powerful hot waterfall pouring from a cave ceiling opening into a deep pool; behind and beneath it carved stone niches let guests sit under focused massage streams; a walkway passes behind the curtain of falling water, lit amber from behind, spray and mist everywhere.

Attraction 10, WAVE GROTTO: a huge sea cave connected to the ocean, transformed into a heated wave pool; gentle rolling waves crash onto a black volcanic sand beach inside the cave, glowing teal water, stalactites, an opening to the moonlit sea in the distance, lounge beds with lanterns on the black sand.

A private guest suite carved into the volcano wall: minimalist Japanese room with tatami, low futon, washi screens slid open onto a private stone onsen tub filled by a small trickling stream from the mountain above, the tub on a ledge overlooking the misty cascade terraces far below at dusk. Warm, intimate, ultra luxurious.

A brand identity and materials mood board for "KAZAN-YU 火山湯" volcano spa, laid out on a dark slate surface: a minimalist logo combining a volcano silhouette and a hot spring steam symbol, indigo yukata with the logo, a basalt key token, a ceramic tea cup, a hinoki wood bucket, swatches labeled "OBSIDIAN", "BASALT", "ONSEN TEAL", "LANTERN AMBER", "NEON MAGENTA", a paper lantern, a menu card. Clean, elegant, photographed from above.
